error.busy_homey: Homey's Bluetooth is busy. The command was not sent — try again shortly.
error.busy_device: The AquaClean is handling another request. Try again shortly.
error.timeout: The AquaClean connected but did not answer. Close the Geberit Home app, move the proxy closer, and try again.
error.command_uncertain: The command was sent but the AquaClean did not confirm it. It has probably been carried out — check the toilet before pressing again, because pressing again reverses it.
error.no_proxy: No Bluetooth proxy configured. Open the app settings and enter the address of your ESPHome proxy.
error.unsupported_control: This control is not available on the AquaClean.
error.not_kept_profile: The AquaClean kept {{stored}} for profile {{profile}} instead of {{value}}.
error.service_missing: The Geberit service was not found on the device.
error.gatt_incomplete: The AquaClean Bluetooth profile is incomplete. Missing: {{missing}}.
error.not_found: The AquaClean was not found. Close the Geberit Home app, wake the toilet, and check that the proxy is within range.
error.multiple_found: Several AquaClean devices were found, but the paired one was not responding.
error.deleted: The device has been removed from Homey.

unavailable.no_contact: No contact with the AquaClean. Checking the Bluetooth proxy and the distance to the toilet usually helps.

state.do_not_trust: the values below cannot be trusted

start.title: Before you start
start.intro: Homey does not talk to the AquaClean directly. It goes through an ESP32 running ESPHome as a Bluetooth proxy, so a few things need to be in place.
start.step_proxy: Flash an ESP32 with ESPHome. A complete, tested configuration is on GitHub at github.com/torp93/homey-geberit-aquaclean, as esphome/geberit-aquaclean-proxy.yaml.
start.step_wifi: Before flashing, put your WiFi name and password into ESPHome’s secrets.yaml as wifi_ssid and wifi_password.
start.step_range: Place the ESP32 within a few metres of the toilet, with as little concrete and metal in between as possible.
start.step_address: The next screen asks for the ESP32’s address. Use a fixed IP or a DHCP reservation so it does not move.
start.step_app: Close the Geberit Home app on your phone. The toilet accepts only one Bluetooth connection at a time.
start.note: Once that is done, continue and Homey will look for the toilet.

proxy.title: Bluetooth proxy
proxy.intro: Enter the address of the ESP32 running ESPHome. Use a fixed IP or a DHCP reservation so it does not move later.
proxy.invalidHost: Enter a valid IP address or hostname.
proxy.noProxy: Connected, but this device has no bluetooth_proxy enabled. Add bluetooth_proxy and esp32_ble_tracker to its ESPHome config.
proxy.untested: Saved without a successful test — the search may find nothing.

result.already_added: Found {{name}}, but it is already added to Homey. To pair it again, remove the existing device first. Otherwise you can close this and keep using the one you have.
result.none_advertising: The proxy is working and sees {{count}} Bluetooth devices, but none of them is an AquaClean. Close the Geberit Home app on your phone, press a button on the toilet to wake it, and try again.
result.proxy_silent: The Bluetooth proxy reported no devices at all. Check that the ESP32 is powered on, reachable at the address you entered, and running bluetooth_proxy.

calibrate.title: Calibrate lid position
calibrate.intro: Adjusts the resting position of the lid and seat. Watch the toilet while you do this — nothing here is reported back by the device.
calibrate.warning: Starting this puts the toilet into a service mode: normal operation stops and its own remote is locked out until the routine finishes. Close this screen and the app finishes it for you, keeping the position currently shown.
calibrate.step2: Step 2 — adjust while watching the lid
calibrate.started: Calibration started. Use Raise and Lower, then save.
calibrate.saved: Position saved. The toilet is back to normal operation.
